A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EarthquakeNPP benchmark. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: v2 reports original likelihood evaluations, simulated CSEP forecasts, computational results, and synthetic-catalog experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds a training-window control, a Japanese-protocol comparison, simulation timings, and forecast diagnostics.

M1.justification: The five NPP architectures and the ETAS formulation and estimation procedure remain unchanged. ETAS* changes the training window, while the proposed magnitude, memory, and training-objective improvements remain future recommendations.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ComCat, SCEDC, White, the two QTM regions, complete and incomplete synthetic ETAS catalogs, and Japan_Deprecated. The added comparison with the original Japanese benchmark varies partitioning and event exclusion within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Likelihood comparisons retain NSTPP, DeepSTPP, AutoSTPP, ETAS, and Poisson; CSEP comparisons retain ETAS, SMASH, and DSTPP. ETAS* is the existing comparator under a different training setting, rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: v3 adds a training-only ETAS control in Appendix C, evaluates the original Japanese protocol alongside the chronological version in Table 4, and benchmarks runtime using batches of 100 simulations. The main dataset splits, likelihood metrics, and daily CSEP evaluation design remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative checks of Japanese benchmark inflation and ETAS training-window sensitivity. It replaces cumulative spatial information-gain curves with geographic diagnostics and expands the existing earthquake case analysis into full-period temporal and spatial forecast analyses across datasets.

E5.justification: Both versions report NPP means and standard deviations from three runs and retain the CSEP simulation counts, significance conventions, and forecast intervals. New runtime summaries describe variation across forecast days, not additional seed-based uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 2 revises likelihood estimates, and Table 2 changes all fifteen number-test pass rates: for example, ETAS on ComCat changes from 85.1% to 95.8%, and DSTPP on SCEDC from 0.0% to 27.4%. Other Table 2 statistics remain unchanged. v3 also adds Japanese-protocol information gains, training-window results, simulation timings, and diagnostic findings; the revised pass rates are not explained as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix D.2 revises v2 Appendix C.2's theoretical argument that DeepSTPP and AutoSTPP permit fast Hawkes branching simulation. It explains why history-dependent kernels prevent independent branching and identifies AutoSTPP's thinning-bound problem. The numbered mathematical definitions and equations are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an earthquake benchmarking platform, and the headline conclusion remains that none of the five tested NPPs outperforms ETAS overall. The revised abstract makes the curation of existing resources more explicit without changing that contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive ETAS limitations involving inhibition, stress relaxation, foreshocks, and isotropic triggering. It expands interpretations of model-specific forecast failures and develops new arguments about next-event training versus sequence evaluation and incorporating empirical scaling laws, beyond v2's magnitude and memory recommendations.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies duplicate-location removal, explains the retained restriction on SMASH magnitude forecasting, and supplies inference and simulation timing details. Hardware, software versions, training-time disclosures, and code access remain substantially unchanged. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: The new NPP overview in Section 2.3 substantially expands architectural positioning, including work by Mei and Eisner, Zuo and colleagues, and Mukherjee and colleagues. Additional stress-release, foreshock, generative-model, and long-context references broaden the motivation and research directions beyond v2's benchmarking-focused discussion.

P1.justification: The conclusion is rewritten into four detailed research directions, background and evaluation explanations are expanded, and related work gains explicit subdivisions. The appendices are reorganized into dedicated training-window, likelihood-analysis, and CSEP-analysis sections, substantially changing the exposition.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template, redraws and separates the main likelihood figures, and changes axes and model ordering. It replaces spatial cumulative curves with maps and adds training-window panels, Japanese-comparison and simulation-time tables, and extensive forecast figures.

improvement.justification: The ETAS training-window control addresses a fairness concern, while expanded diagnostics, limitations, and runtime evidence make the benchmark more useful and better supported. These gains are qualified by an introduced reporting inconsistency: v2 Table 2 and Figure 12 agree on SMASH's ComCat pass rate of 72.4%, whereas v3 Table 2 reports 86.2% while Figure 15 retains 72.4%. This unresolved discrepancy limits confidence in the revised calibration reporting.
